EDIT: Spontaneous question, do you speak different languages in the Czech Republic and Slovakia?

The languages are mutually intelligeble so very few people actually make the effort to speak the other language unless they are actually living in the other country, but even then some immigrants don't really make the effort, for example my hairdresser still spoke to me in Slovak everytime I went to see here in Czechia. When I went to Slovakia I just spoke Czech and Slovak tourists do the same thing here as we can understand each other very easily, although I have to admit that it's a bit harder for me as a young person than for people who actually grew up in Czechoslovakia. But unless they are speaking really fast I can still understand 90-95% percent. Poles do the same thing but reaching a mutual understanding is a bit more complicated but can be done if both parties speak slowly. There the level of understanding would be maybe 60-70% but higher if I was reading a text and I had some time to read through it. Slavic languages are truly a family so you can always understand the general message.
